questions.q: What real problem does versioning a Scripted REST API actually solve?
options: It lets a developer change a resource's request/response shape in a new version without breaking integrations still calling the old version
It is required before any Scripted REST API can be activated at all
It makes a Scripted REST API run faster under heavy load
It replaces the need for required roles on the API definition
questions.explain: Versioning exists so a shape change can ship as a new version while existing callers on the old version keep getting the old shape, unchanged.

questions.q: An API's base path is /api/x_acme_eqchk, with Version records v1 and v2. What does each Version record contribute?
options: Nothing visible in the URL — versions only change internal script behavior
A required role that overrides the API definition's own role setting
Its own base-path segment, inserted between the API's base path and each Resource's relative path
A completely separate sys_ws_definition record with no shared base path
questions.explain: A Version adds its own segment (v1, v2) to the URL, e.g. /api/x_acme_eqchk/v1/... and /api/x_acme_eqchk/v2/..., both live at once.

questions.q: A v2 Resource needs to return an extra checked_out field that v1 doesn't have. How should that be built?
options: By adding an if branch inside v1's existing script that checks the request's version
By deleting v1's Resource once v2 is ready, since only one version can exist at a time
It cannot be done — a Scripted REST API's response shape can never change once published
As a separate Resource script under the v2 Version, leaving v1's script untouched
questions.explain: v2 gets its own Resource and script under its own Version — v1's script stays exactly as it was, so v1's behavior never changes.

questions.q: Given GET /api/x_acme_eqchk/v1/equipment/{sys_id} and a later v2, what happens to the v1 URL once v2 ships?
options: It is merged into v2 and must use the new required fields
It keeps working exactly as before — versioning is additive, nothing about v1 changes or gets disabled
It stops working immediately once v2 is activated
It automatically redirects every caller to the v2 response shape
questions.explain: Adding a new Version doesn't remove or alter an existing one — both base paths stay live until a team deliberately retires one.

questions.q: What real coordination cost does versioning let a team avoid, per this lesson?
options: The need to ever write more than one Resource for an entire API
The need to ever use response.setStatus() for error cases
A breaking change rolled out to every calling system at once, on one team's timeline, with no way for callers to opt out
The need for any required role on the Scripted REST API definition
questions.explain: Without versioning, a shape change would hit every caller simultaneously; versioning lets each integration migrate to the new version on its own schedule.
